newsitem.title: USA: Community groups protest NationsBank merger.
newsitem.headline: Community groups protest NationsBank merger.

text.p: A coalition of community groups has filed a formal challenge to the application of NationsBank Corp to acquire Boatmen's Bancshares Inc, one of the groups, Inner City Press/Community on the Move, said.
Inner City Press, based in the Bronx, N.Y., said other groups in the protest include the New Mexico Alliance and the Mid-South Peace and Justice Center of Memphis.
Inner city Press said the protest was filed with the Federal Reserve Board, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Inner City Press said it was seeking disclosure of branch closings that would occur in Memphis and in Austin, Texas, as a result of the proposed merger.

It also said NationsBank has said publicly that it has surpassed a $10 billion community lending commitment made in 1991 when it acquired C&S Sovran Bank. Inner City Press said it questioned how much of the total included lending by the company's NationsCredit sub-prime finance company.
NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., was not available for comment.
NationsBank's proposed merger with St. Louis-based Boatmen's, for about $9 billion in cash and stock, would be the third-largest U.S. bank merger ever.
